summary: BC's northernmost lighthouse, on a bare island in Chatham Sound near the Alaska border, lit in 1906 after the wreck of the collier Bristol and rebuilt in concrete in the 1950s.

evidence.quote: The lighthouse is located on Green Island in Chatham Sound, about 40 kilometres northwest of Prince Rupert, British Columbia. It is British Columbia’s northernmost lighthouse.
Just 5 kilometres from the Alaskan border, it is the first notable landmark that is seen as marine traffic enters Canada.
In 1906, the Green Island lightstation was established after a number of shipwrecks including the wrecks of the steamer Mexico and the collier Bristol.
The Klondike Gold Rush of 1897 resulted in an increased volume of marine traffic in the region.
The Green Island Lighthouse was constructed in 1956 and is the second lighthouse on the site, replacing the original tower constructed in 1906.

notes_for_editor: Most keeper and event detail rests on Lighthouse Friends (copyrighted; paraphrased), which cites departmental reports, the Daily Colonist (21 Oct 1909) and Moran's 1929 report, none read directly. Bristol: the 1903 report says reef off 'Grey Island' off N. Dundas Island; LF/CoastView say Green Island (Gray Island is also mentioned near the station in the Moran account), so the identification is unresolved. LF spells the 1963 keeper Wolski in its list and Wolksi in the text; the Pare dates are 1996 in the list. No newspapers (BC papers not in Chronicling America) or Canadian keeper tables read; the marine_ca keeper tables could add 1906-1923 names. The 1905 report's 44 ft is to the top of the lantern ventilator. Height_m 13.4 converts that. Staffing in 2024 not confirmed by the Coast Guard release, which does not name the 25 stations. Fact-check 2026-10-27: Grey/Gray/Green Island identification left open; ownership is from LF only (List of Lights gives no owner).
